entry_points.text: Unified tickless wake prefers full kick else idle path. Control-group iteration refreshes active clamp accounting for all attached tasks.
Remote tick start uses cross-call, local programs directly. Queue initialization sets up cross-call plus timer.

exports.text: Clamp queries report effective bounds: runqueue prefers highest occupied bucket else idle default; task uses active annotated value when accounted else computes effective.
Completion wakes one waiter or broadcasts sticky done. Waits cover uninterruptible, interruptible, killable, caller state with timeouts, plus IO variants, try and done query.
Core hold is refcounted with mutex enable and deferred disable. Deferred wake queues insert once atomically and drain in order; direct wake uses normal state.
Lazy preemption selects lazy or regular flag; remote reschedule locks online targets. Helpers report cache node, idle, isolated sets, group no-op, task presence and current occupant.
Idle wake notifies remotes polling-aware; tickless-full kicks stopped ticks, offline satisfied. Isolated representative prefers caller else online member, warning once if none.

hazards.text: After release-publishing not-on-runqueue, a waker may migrate the task, so callers must not touch it. Tickless cross-call warns without kick flag, processing soft work only when idle.
Effective clamps cap requests by parent and protection by limit, update changed buckets, prune unchanged subtrees and refresh members; needs clamp mutex under RCU, warning otherwise.

invariants.text: Clamp release skips disabled/delayed cases, else releases each identity with guarded decrement and aggregate recompute from top occupied bucket or idle; reinc refreshes actives.
Root refresh propagates system controls; usage enables on first use. Sysctl validates bounds, restores on failure and propagates defaults; thread sync orders creation.
Dequeue measures delay from enqueue stamp then clears it, tracking totals and extrema. Stall dequeue skips disabled, state-saving or switch-handled cases, else clears states.

Donor reset returns via prev/next switch, repoints donor, keeps push callback and reschedules. Switch moves deadline ownership, warns on mismatch; current/donor compare pointers and proxy defaults enabled.
Queued wakeup needs policy allow, excludes stop, checks active/affinity, queues non-sharing/idle remotes never local. State match reports direct/deferred hits; cache uses LLC, polling set uses CAS.

Core order is stop, deadline service, numeric, extension/fair squash, idle. Tree sorts by cookie then urgency; ties use deadlines, adjusted virtual time, or extension callbacks, skipping throttled tasks.
Tick stops without deadline, multiple RR, constrained fair, or negative extension. Extension denies in bypass/rescue else per-queue flag; fair maps via entity or queue with quota check.
Weight uses idle magnitude or priority table; idle is single policy. Group walk visits down/up with early exit; NUMA intersects locality under RCU; features are bitmask with static keys.

locks.text: Queue mutators need caller-held lock. Lock pairs spin with preemption pin; task pinning revalidates CPU, spins while migrating, retries on pointer change to avoid wrong queue.
Core flip locks siblings under hotplug guard, waits in-flight picks, updates enabled flags. Double lock orders by core then CPU with interrupts off, preserving skip flags.
Completion uses wait-queue lock with interrupts disabled; fast unsynchronized check precedes recheck under lock before sleep or consume.
Clamp updates hold queue/inheritance locks; hierarchy needs clamp mutex under RCU; rescue needs queue lock; wait-channel, state and housekeeping deref need inheritance or hotplug/cpuset protection.

state_machines.text: Wakeup tries async remote wakelist with clock sync and pending marks first, returning unlocked; else locks target, updates clock, activates and unlocks.
Wait sleeps while not done, checking signals, preparing waiter, sleeping unlocked, relocking; on exit detaches, consumes one unit except sticky broadcast, normalizing zero timeout.
Schedule entry defers tick; exit applies pending start, cancels idle timers, performs rearm. Callback ticks donor under lock without restart; restart when unqueued, running, or expiry shifted.
Fork clears active clamp markers, optionally resets requests, post-fork syncs realtime default; deactivation marks migrating until later enqueue clears it.

structs.text: Queues show aggregates, current/donor/server, callbacks, counts, clock and tickless flags; tasks show presence, class, affinity, wake nodes, states, clamps and timing; waiters link once, groups via container.
Tick modes are none, defer, start, rearm with deferred start/rearm intents; slices clamp to ten thousand nanoseconds, rearm needs five thousand shift. Queues init idle with unrestricted clamps.
